purpose: instrument check before registration: does a two-sided word target produce cost parity, and does the style manipulation survive being pinned

A.text:
The Meridian Review 2026 round evaluates each manuscript against ten rules and returns one of three outcomes. R1: at least twenty‑two pages (twenty-two suffices). R2: use the official template or provide ≥ three years documented revision history. R3: a Tier‑1 venue presentation < eighteen months before 1 March 2026 disqualifies; exactly eighteen months does not qualify. R4: acceptance in an earlier Meridian round blocks handling unless five full years have passed; exactly five years is acceptable. R5: a paired submission may contain only two manuscripts; both must meet R1 and R2, and at least one of the pair must satisfy R3. R6: Track D papers are exempt from R2 but require exactly two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient. R7: any manuscript with an open retraction notice is automatically rejected, overriding all other rules, including R9. R8: figures must be 8–45; for paired submissions the maximum rises to 70 while the minimum stays 8. R9: if a paper fails R8 only by having < 8 figures, it is padded to eight and labelled PADDED; any excess beyond the maximum causes RETURN. R10: a withdrawal does not count as an acceptance for R4 but resets the R3 clock, making the presentation date the withdrawal date.

HANDLED means all applicable rules are met; RETURNED means an applicable rule fails (excluding PADDED); PADDED applies only to the short‑figure case that otherwise meets every requirement.

The Meridian Review round evaluates each manuscript by ten numbered requirements and returns one of three verdicts.

R1: at least twenty‑two pages (twenty‑two counts). R2: must use the official template or show at least three years of documented revision history. R3: Tier‑1 venue papers are rejected unless presented more than eighteen months before 1 March 2026; eighteen months does not qualify. R4: a manuscript accepted in an earlier Meridian round is rejected if fewer than five years have passed since that acceptance; five years is acceptable.

R5 allows a paired submission of exactly two manuscripts; both must satisfy R1 and R2, and at least one must also satisfy R3. R6 applies to Track D papers: they are exempt from R2 but require two endorsements.

R7 states any manuscript with an open retraction notice is not handled, overriding all other rules including R9. R8 limits figures to eight‑to‑forty‑five, inclusive; a paired submission may have up to seventy figures while keeping same minimum eight.

R9: if a paper fails R8 only by falling below the minimum, it is padded to eight figures and receives PADDED; exceeding the maximum causes RETURNED. R10 notes that a prior‑round withdrawal does not count as an acceptance for R4 but resets R3 clock to withdrawal date.

If every applicable rule is met verdict is HANDLED; otherwise RETURNED, except when PADDED applies under R9.

The Meridian Review system gives one verdict per submission as 1 March 2026 deadline. Manuscripts must be at least twenty‑two pages; exactly twenty‑two satisfies length rule (R1). It must either use template or provide documented revision history covering three years or more (R2). Presentation at a Tier‑1 venue is allowed only if it occurred more than eighteen months before the deadline; exactly eighteen months does not qualify (R3). Acceptance in a prior Meridian round disqualifies a paper unless at least five years have passed since that round; exactly five years is acceptable (R4). A paired submission may contain exactly two manuscripts; both must meet R1 and R2, and at least one must also satisfy R3 (R5). Track D submissions are exempt from R2 but must carry exactly two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient, and it applies only to R2 (R6). Any manuscript with an open retraction notice is rejected, overriding other rule including R9 (R7). Figure count must be between eight and forty‑five inclusive; a paired submission may have up to seventy figures while keeping same minimum (R8). If a paper falls short of minimum, it is padded to eight and receives PADDED, but excess over the maximum yields RETURNED (R9). Withdrawals do not count as acceptances for R4 and reset venue clock for R3 to withdrawal date (R10). Outcomes are HANDLED, RETURNED, or PADDED.

The Meridian Review handling system evaluates each submission on 1 March 2026 using numbered rules and yields one of three verdicts: HANDLED, RETURNED or PADDED.

R1 demands at least twenty‑two pages; satisfies it. R2 requires either official template or documented revision history covering at least three years. R3 disallows a paper presented at a Tier‑1 venue unless that presentation was more than eighteen months before the deadline (eighteen months fails). R4 rejects papers accepted in a prior Meridian round if fewer than five years have passed; five years is acceptable. R5 allows a paired submission of exactly two manuscripts; three or more are prohibited. Both must meet R1 and R2, and at least one must satisfy R3.

R6 applies only to Track D: it waives R2 but obliges exactly two endorsements (one is insufficient) and does not waive rule. R7 makes manuscript with an open retraction notice RETURNED, overriding all rules including R9. R8 limits figures to a minimum of eight and a maximum of forty‑five; paired submissions may have up to seventy figures while keeping same lower bound.

R9 pads a submission that fails R8 by having fewer than eight figures, raising it to eight and resulting in PADDED; excess figures cause RETURNED. R10 notes that a prior‑round withdrawal does not count as an acceptance for R4 and resets R3 venue clock to withdrawal date.

Acceptance in any previous Meridian round disqualifies the work unless at least five years have passed since that round; precisely five years elapsed is sufficient. A paired submission may consist of exactly two papers; each must meet the page‑length and format conditions, while at least one of the pair must also satisfy venue‑overlap timing. Track D submissions are exempt from format rule but require exactly two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient and does not waive any other rule. Any manuscript with an open retraction notice is returned, overriding provision including figure adjustments. Figure count must be between eight and forty‑five inclusive for single papers and may rise to seventy for a pair; minimum remains eight. A prior‑round withdrawal does not count as an acceptance for the five‑year rule and resets venue clock, making the withdrawal date the presentation date.

Manuscripts must contain at least twenty‑two pages; a manuscript of exactly twenty‑two pages meets the length requirement. For format, a submission is acceptable only if it either follows the official template or includes documented revision history covering three or more years; lacking both makes it fail format. Venue overlap applies solely to presentations at Tier‑1 venues: the presentation must have occurred more than eighteen months before 1 March 2026; a presentation exactly eighteen months prior does not satisfy the rule, while anything earlier does. Prior‑round acceptance is disallowed unless five full years have passed since that round; exactly five years elapsed is sufficient, fewer than five years is not. Paired submissions are limited to two manuscripts; each member of the pair must meet both length and format requirements, and at least one member must satisfy the venue‑overlap condition; the other may fail that particular rule. Track D removes the format requirement but imposes a need for exactly two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient and does not affect any other rule. Any manuscript with an open retraction notice is returned, overriding every other provision including figure adjustments. Figure count must lie between eight and forty‑five inclusive; paired submissions may have up to seventy figures. If a submission falls short of the minimum figure count it is padded and labelled PADDED, but any excess beyond the maximum causes return.

R1: manuscript must be at least twenty‑two pages; twenty-two passes, fewer fails (RETURNED).

R2: either the template is used or revision history spans three years. Without both the paper is RETURNED unless it is Track D (see R6).

R3: a Tier‑1 venue presentation disqualifies the manuscript unless it occurred more than eighteen months before 1 March 2026; eighteen months does not qualify.

R4: acceptance in an earlier Meridian round blocks the manuscript unless at least five years have elapsed; five years is acceptable.

R5: paired submissions are allowed for two manuscripts. Both must meet R1 and R2; at least one also meets R3. Other pair size fails.

R6: Track D papers are exempt from R2 but must carry two endorsements—one endorsement causes RETURNED; no other rule is waived.

R7: any manuscript with an open retraction notice is RETURNED.

R8: figure count must be eight to forty‑five inclusive for single submissions; paired submissions may have seventy, needing at least eight.

R9: if a paper falls short of minimum in R8 it is PADDED to eight figures and receives verdict PADDED, provided no other rule fails; exceeding maximum yields RETURNED.

R10: a withdrawal does not count as an acceptance for R4 and resets R3 clock to withdrawal date.

If none are violated the manuscript is HANDLED; RETURNED except for the low‑figure violation in R9, which results in PADDED.

Length demands at least twenty‑two pages; exactly twenty‑two passes, fewer fails. Format is satisfied only if the manuscript either uses the official template or supplies documented revision history spanning three or more years; lacking both disqualifies it. Venue overlap concerns Tier‑1 presentations: the presentation must have occurred more than eighteen months before 1 March 2026; exactly eighteen months does not count, so any ≤ 18 months fails this rule. Prior‑round acceptance is excluded unless five full years have passed since that round; five years exactly is acceptable, fewer fails. Paired submissions are permitted for exactly two manuscripts; three or more are prohibited. Each member of a pair must meet Length and Format individually, while at least one of the two must satisfy the venue‑overlap condition; the other may violate it. Track D lifts only the Format requirement and instead requires exactly two endorsements; one endorsement is insufficient and does not waive any other rule. An open retraction overrides every provision and forces RETURNED regardless of R9. Figure count must be between eight and forty‑five inclusive, except a pair may have up to seventy figures. If the count falls below the minimum, the submission is PADDED; if it exceeds the maximum, it is RETURNED. A withdrawal in a prior round replaces the original presentation date for R3, treating the withdrawal date as the effective venue date.
